checked.found: Domesticated Cucurbita pepo seeds at Guila Naquitz dated about 10,000 calibrated years ago (about 8000 BCE); UNESCO gives about 8000 BC.
Cacao use at Santa Ana-La Florida (Ecuador, upper Amazon) about 5,300 years ago, i.e. about 3300 BCE (Zarrillo et al. 2018).
Most sources put the founding of Monte Alban at about 500 BCE.

Preclassic peak from about 300 BCE; La Danta is among the largest pyramids by volume. Year is the approximate start of the peak, as the spine notes. The first results did not directly cover this card.
Sources vary (first settlement from about 400 BCE, monumental city from about 100 BCE); 100 BCE is the commonly cited founding of the city. Not directly confirmed in this pass beyond the spine note.

Chiapa de Corzo Stela 2 is generally cited as the earliest contemporaneous Long Count inscription, 36 BCE, though damaged and not certain; the style is Epi-Olmec rather than strictly Maya, and Takalik Abaj Stela 2 is a disputed possible rival. Description's 'Maya calendar's Long Count' is acceptable.

Wikipedia and the spine use about 250 CE, but the sources in the search gave about 290 CE (carbon date), about 300 CE (Encyclopedia.com) and about 350 CE (visitor guide). The 250 date is not confirmed; the other claims (gold, turquoise, sacrificed attendants, intact tomb) are supported.
Siyaj K'ak' arrived at Tikal on 16 January 378 CE and Tikal's king died the same day; sources describe the Teotihuacan link.
Altar Q's first date is 5 September 426 CE for K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' (arrival in the valley 152 days later); dynasty lasted nearly 400 years.
The 'Great Fire' of the civic-ceremonial core is placed about 550 CE (archaeomagnetic 550 +/- 25), with a 70-80% population decline afterward; some scholars place it as late as the 600s.

562 CE is agreed: Wak Chan K'awiil of Tikal was defeated and sacrificed. Sources differ on whether Calakmul or Caracol (as Calakmul's ally) struck; the card's 'alliance' wording is consistent with both.
Pakal died in 683 CE and was buried in the Temple of the Inscriptions. Confirmed from the spine source and background knowledge; not separately searched.
Wikipedia gives c. 732 CE for Temple I over Burial 116 of Jasaw Chan K'awiil I; other sources vary (727, burial 734, completion 740-750). The 732 figure is the standard one.
Wikipedia gives construction about 850 CE; other sources say between 850 and 900, with the Chimu state starting about 900.

987 is cited as a traditional date, but sources attach it to different events (Itza control, a Toltec takeover, the Mayapan league). The city's rise is more usually placed from about 600 CE through the 900s, so the single year is not confirmed.
Traditional founding by Manco Capac is put at about 1200 CE (some sources say 1100); the description is framed 'By tradition'.
Pachacuti is traditionally dated to 1438 after defeating the Chanka; not separately searched in this pass.
Chimor's fall to the Inca is placed about 1470 CE in the Chan Chan and Chimor sources. 'Its richest rival' is mild embellishment; the first results did not specifically confirm it.
Axayacatl of Tenochtitlan defeated Moquihuix and absorbed Tlatelolco in 1473, taking over its market and tribute.
Templo Mayor rededication under Ahuitzotl in 1487, with traditional accounts of thousands of sacrifices (description says 'said to'). Not separately searched.
Moctezuma II became huey tlatoani in 1502, the ninth Aztec tlatoani, and was later held captive by the Spaniards. Not separately searched.
